title: Six Short Pieces
identity: Lawrence Moss's Six Short Pieces is a 1993 work for E-flat alto saxophone and piano, published by Roncorp in 1995, dedicated to Reggie Jackson and Jessica Krasch. The UPV dissertation explicitly lists six separate pieces: Rounds, Blur, Broadway Boogie-Woogie, Chinese Lullaby, Introduction, and Jazzy. Its printed p.614 reproduces the opening score of Rounds.

evidence.claim: Dissertation states six movements, separately numbering Introduction as no.5 and Jazzy as no.6; it reproduces page 1 of Rounds for E-flat alto saxophone and piano.
evidence.source_name: UPV dissertation on jazz in the classical saxophone repertoire

evidence.claim: In the reproduced Rounds opening, the score marks Leggiero, quarter=96, and p then pp; both alto saxophone and piano parts are shown.
NYPL American Music Center collection finding aid lists the published score for E-flat alto saxophone and piano.
evidence.source_name: New York Public Library finding aid

evidence.claim: Retailer lists alto saxophone and piano, Northeastern Music Publications; its grade label is vendor metadata only.

score_observations.observation: Printed p.614 reproduces Rounds p.1. The saxophone line begins Leggiero at quarter=96, with quick beamed figures and dynamics p to pp; piano has independent moving figures beneath.

review_focus: Inference from the inspected excerpt: the opening Rounds combines light beamed saxophone figures with an independently moving piano line and soft dynamics. The excerpt does not establish demands across the other five pieces.
collection_flag: Published original saxophone/piano work; dissertation dates it 1993 and publication 1995.
gaps: Only the opening of Rounds was inspected; no score details are available here for the other five pieces.
UPV site blocks automated page opening, but the locally available dissertation was read and its score figure inspected.
